html:
An Omani Arab and Swahili trader from Zanzibar, born Hamad bin Muhammad al-Murjabi, who became the most powerful merchant in the interior of East and Central Africa.

From the 1860s his armed caravans pushed inland from the coast to the upper Congo, trading in ivory and enslaved people. He built a trading state in the eastern Congo, around Kasongo, and his men were feared across the region. European explorers relied on him: he met David Livingstone and helped Henry Morton Stanley on his journey down the Congo in 1876 to 1877.

In 1887 Leopold II made him governor of the Stanley Falls district of the Congo Free State, a deal between two rival powers. He went back to Zanzibar in 1890 and wrote his memoirs in Swahili. Soon after, the Free State fought and destroyed the Arab and Swahili traders he had led. He died in Zanzibar in 1905.
